images.caption: Nott Memorial Hall, built in 1858 on the campus of Union College in Schenectady, New York, United States, commemorates Eliphalet Nott, president of Union from 1804 to 1866 (for which he became, and still remains, the longest serving college or university president in United States history). The structure was placed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1972 and subsequently became a National Historic Landmark in 1986. It is currently used as a student lounge and study area, a display space for art, and for special events on campus.
images.alt: Nott Memorial Hall, built in 1858 on the campus of Union College in Schenectady, New York, United States, commemorates Eliphalet Nott, president of Union from 1804 to 1866 (for which he became, and still remains, the longest serving college or university president in United States history). The structure was placed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1972 and subsequently became a National Historic Landmark in 1986. It is currently used as a student lounge and study area, a display space for art, and for special events on campus.

images.caption: The Adelphia Hotel located at 361–365 Broadway in Saratoga Springs, New York, was built in 1877 and is the last surviving hotel in the city from the 19th century. The porch, which features slender columns and open spandrels became known as the "Saratoga porch" because it was typical of the time and place. The hotel is part of the Broadway Historic District, which was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1979.
